ai.description: The Dudhwa Tree Frog (Rhacophoridae) measures 25–30 mm. It is pale yellow to brownish with a distinct dark brown interorbital triangle and granular skin. It features translucent, unpigmented toe discs.
ai.identificationRemarks: The *Chirixalus dudhwaensis* is best distinguished by the distinct, dark-brown longitudinal stripes on its dorsum, which are absent in most other similar Indian tree frogs.
ai.habitat: The Dudhwa tree frog inhabits moist deciduous forests and swampy grasslands in the Himalayan foothills, typically found at low to moderate altitudes near water bodies.
ai.behavior: The Dudhwa tree frog is primarily nocturnal, remaining hidden in vegetation during the day and emerging at night to forage for small insects.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Chirixalus dudhwaensis* breeds during the monsoon (June–August), depositing clutches of 100–150 eggs in foam nests attached to vegetation overhanging water.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Dudhwa Tree Frog is endemic to the Terai region of northern India, specifically occurring in the Dudhwa National Park area of Uttar Pradesh at low elevations.
ai.callDescription: The Dudhwa Tree Frog emits a series of short, high-pitched "peep" notes, typically heard during the monsoon season from vegetation surrounding stagnant water bodies.
